experiences.name: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel
experiences.description: Explore one of the world's greatest art collections, culminating in Michelangelo's breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling. Book skip-the-line tickets in advance to maximize your time among thousands of masterpieces spanning centuries of artistic achievement.

experiences.name: Trastevere Food & Wine Walking Tour
experiences.description: Wander through Rome's most charming medieval neighborhood sampling supplì (fried rice balls), artisanal cheeses, cured meats, and local Frascati wine at family-run trattorias and market stalls. A guided tour brings the culinary history of the city to life.
experiences.location: Trastevere, right bank of the Tiber

experiences.name: Borghese Gallery Art Experience
experiences.description: Discover Bernini's stunning baroque sculptures and Caravaggio's dramatic paintings in this intimate villa gallery. Entry is strictly timed and limited to 360 visitors per session, creating an exclusive and unhurried art experience unlike any other in Rome.

experiences.name: Testaccio Market Culinary Exploration
experiences.description: Dive into Rome's authentic food culture at this beloved local market. Sample offal-based Roman street food, fresh pasta, seasonal produce, and artisan cheeses. Visit the nearby slaughterhouse-turned-contemporary-art-space MACRO Testaccio for a culture-food fusion experience.

experiences.name: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Sunset Visit
experiences.description: Walk through the ancient heart of the Roman Empire as golden hour light bathes millennia-old ruins in a warm glow. The Palatine Hill offers sweeping panoramic views over the Forum below, providing an unmatched blend of history, archaeology, and visual artistry.
experiences.location: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum, Historic Centre

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 16:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Rome (Georgia) airport at 16:00 on Condor flight. Collect luggage, arrange ground transport, and check in to La Quinta by Wyndham Rome at 15 Chateau Drive. Freshen up and get settled in your room.
day_by_day.evening: Take a relaxed evening stroll around the local area near the hotel to get your bearings. Explore the nearby streets of Rome, GA, and pick up any essentials from a nearby grocery or convenience store to stock up on snacks and drinks for the week ahead.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or at the airport
meals.lunch: Meal on the flight or at the airport
meals.dinner: Zaxby's or Chick-fil-A near Chateau Drive for a quick, affordable first-night dinner (~$8-12). Alternatively, grab groceries from a nearby Walmart or Kroger for a budget-friendly in-room meal.

day_by_day.notes: Since the hotel is La Quinta by Wyndham in Rome, Georgia (USA) rather than Rome, Italy, this itinerary is tailored to Rome, GA and its surrounding region. Day 1 is intentionally light given the 4 PM arrival. Check if the hotel offers a free continental breakfast for the following mornings to save on meal costs.

day_by_day.morning: Start with the hotel's complimentary breakfast if available. Head to Downtown Rome, GA (about 5-10 min drive) and visit the Rome Area History Museum (free or low-cost entry, ~$5). Explore the historic downtown area, including the iconic Clock Tower and the Three Rivers confluence at Riverside Park — a beautiful and completely free outdoor attraction.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Chieftains Museum / Major Ridge Home (National Historic Landmark, ~$5 entry), which offers fascinating art and cultural history exhibits about Cherokee heritage. Afterward, walk along the Riverwalk trail along the Oostanaula River — free, scenic, and great for photos. Stop by local shops and galleries in the downtown arts district.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Broad Street in downtown Rome for the local dining scene. Browse any open art galleries or pop-up events in the downtown arts corridor.

meals.breakfast: Hotel complimentary breakfast or grab a coffee and pastry from a local café (~$4-6)
meals.lunch: Harvest Moon Café on Broad Street — local favorite with affordable lunch options (~$10-14)
meals.dinner: El Sombrero Mexican Restaurant in Rome, GA — generous portions at budget-friendly prices (~$10-15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Rome, GA sits at the confluence of three rivers and has a charming, walkable downtown. Wear comfortable shoes and bring water — June temperatures average around 30°C. Apply sunscreen and consider a hat for afternoon outdoor activities.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, visit the Shorter University Art Gallery or check local listings for any free art exhibitions in the area. Then head to the Rome Little Theatre or local community arts center to see what performances or exhibits are on display. Many community art spaces in Rome, GA offer free or donation-based entry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to nearby Cave Spring (~15 miles, 20 min) to visit Rolater Park and the natural limestone cave — a unique and very affordable attraction (~$2-3 entry). The park also has a natural spring-fed swimming pool, perfect for cooling off in the June heat. Explore the charming small-town antique shops and local art studios in Cave Spring.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Rome and enjoy a leisurely evening. Check local event listings for free outdoor concerts or community events — Rome, GA often hosts summer evening events in its parks and downtown area.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or make your own with groceries (~$3-5)
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch from a local deli or grocery store to enjoy at Rolater Park in Cave Spring (~$6-8)
meals.dinner: Schroeder's New Deli on Broad Street, Rome — known for hearty, affordable sandwiches and local favorites (~$10-13)

day_by_day.notes: Cave Spring is a hidden gem near Rome and very budget-friendly. Bring a swimsuit if you want to use the spring-fed pool at Rolater Park. Check opening hours in advance as some smaller attractions may have limited summer schedules.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning drive to Chattanooga, Tennessee (~1 hour from Rome, GA). Visit the free Coolidge Park on the North Shore and walk across the Walnut Street Bridge. Head to the Hunter Museum of American Art — one of the finest art museums in the Southeast (~$15 entry, free for under 18). The museum sits dramatically on a bluff above the Tennessee River with stunning views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Tennessee Aquarium (optional, ~$35 if budget allows, or admire the exterior and surrounding Riverfront area for free). Walk along the Chattanooga Riverwalk — completely free and beautiful. Browse the local shops and street food vendors along the waterfront.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to Rome, GA in the early evening. Relax at the hotel or explore a local Rome neighborhood you haven't visited yet.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Niedlov's Breadworks in Chattanooga — artisan bakery with affordable sandwiches and pastries (~$9-12)
meals.dinner: Back in Rome, GA: Applebee's or a local pizza spot near the hotel for a relaxed budget dinner (~$10-15)

day_by_day.notes: Chattanooga is an excellent day trip for art and food lovers. The Hunter Museum alone is worth the drive. Gas for the round trip (~120 miles total) will cost approximately $15-18. Check the Hunter Museum website for any free admission days or discount codes before visiting.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Rome Farmers Market (open Sunday mornings, seasonal) to sample local produce, artisan foods, and handmade crafts — free to browse and great for budget food shopping. Pick up fresh local fruit, baked goods, and snacks. Then head to Berry College campus (free to enter) — one of the largest college campuses in the world with beautiful Gothic architecture, wildlife, and scenic grounds perfect for a morning walk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at Lock and Dam Park on the Coosa River — a free outdoor space with river views, walking trails, and picnic areas. Bring your farmers market haul for a riverside picnic. If you enjoy photography, the river and dam make for excellent artistic shots.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Rome's local food scene on Broad Street. Look for any Sunday evening specials or happy hour deals at local restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Fresh items purchased at the Rome Farmers Market (~$5-8)
meals.lunch: Picnic at Lock and Dam Park with farmers market finds (~$5-7 total)
meals.dinner: Mellow Mushroom Rome, GA — creative pizzas in a fun atmosphere with reasonable prices (~$12-16 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Berry College is a must-see — the campus is stunning and completely free to visit. White-tailed deer are commonly spotted on campus. Confirm the farmers market schedule in advance as hours can vary by season. June heat will be significant by midday, so plan outdoor activities for morning and late afternoon.

day_by_day.date: 2027-06-21 (Monday) - Day Trip to Atlanta Art Scene
day_by_day.morning: Drive to Atlanta (~1 hour from Rome, GA) for a full day of world-class art. Visit the High Museum of Art — one of the premier art museums in the American South (~$19.50 general admission, often has discount days). The museum houses an impressive permanent collection including European paintings, American art, folk art, and photography. Spend 2-3 hours exploring.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through Midtown Atlanta and visit the free Atlanta Botanical Garden exterior areas or explore Piedmont Park (free entry). Browse the Virginia-Highland or Little Five Points neighborhoods for street art, murals, and independent galleries — many are free to enter. Atlanta has an incredible street mural scene perfect for art lovers.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to Rome, GA by early evening. Enjoy a quiet dinner near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before early departure
meals.lunch: Ponce City Market food hall in Atlanta — wide variety of affordable options from multiple vendors (~$10-14)
meals.dinner: Back in Rome: Longhorn Steakhouse or Olive Garden near Chateau Drive for a sit-down budget dinner (~$13-18)

day_by_day.notes: Check the High Museum website for any Monday specials or discount admission days — they occasionally offer reduced pricing. The Atlanta street art scene (especially in Cabbagetown and the BeltLine area) is world-class and completely free. Parking in Midtown Atlanta can be expensive; look for street parking or affordable garages (~$5-10).

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a final leisurely breakfast. Take one last walk through Downtown Rome, GA to pick up any souvenirs from local shops or the Rome Area Council for the Arts gift shop. Visit any spots you may have missed during the week — the Forum River Center or the Capitoline Wolf statue replica (Rome, GA has its own replica gifted from Rome, Italy!) are quick and free stops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Pack up and check out of the hotel. Spend any remaining time at a local café or park. If time allows, drive up to Myrtle Hill Cemetery — a historic hilltop cemetery with panoramic views of Rome and the three rivers, completely free and surprisingly beautiful.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the airport or arrange onward transport. Reflect on a wonderful week exploring Rome, Georgia's art, food, and natural beauty.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast or a treat at a local café (~$5-8)
meals.lunch: Broad Street Baking Company or a local sandwich shop for a farewell meal (~$9-12)
meals.dinner: Airport meal or travel snacks purchased from a grocery store before departure (~$5-10)

day_by_day.notes: Rome, GA's Capitoline Wolf statue is a genuine gift from Rome, Italy — a fun and free photo opportunity that connects this Rome to its Italian namesake. Use this final morning to revisit any favorite spots. Keep receipts throughout the trip to track spending against your budget. Total estimated daily budget (excluding accommodation): $30-50/day covering meals, entry fees, and local transport.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 16:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive Rome (Condor flight lands 16:00). Clear customs, collect luggage, and transfer to La Quinta by Wyndham Rome (~30–45 min). Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll around the immediate neighborhood to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Easy first-night wander: head to a nearby piazza for a classic Roman aperitivo (Aperol Spritz or Negroni) at a local bar. Keep the evening relaxed after travel.

meals.breakfast: N/A – in transit
meals.lunch: N/A – in transit / airport meal
meals.dinner: Casual dinner close to the hotel – look for a neighborhood trattoria offering Roman staples like cacio e pepe or tonnarelli alla gricia. Budget ~$20–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Do not over-schedule Day 1. Jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Prioritize rest so you can enjoy full days ahead. Confirm all experience bookings and download offline maps tonight.

day_by_day.morning: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel (book timed-entry tickets in advance for ~9:00 AM opening). Spend 3–4 hours exploring the Raphael Rooms, Gallery of Maps, and culminating in Michelangelo's awe-inspiring Sistine Chapel ceiling. Arrive early to beat crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Vatican, cross the Tiber and explore the Castel Sant'Angelo exterior and the scenic Lungotevere riverside promenade. Rest briefly at a café before heading toward Piazza Navona to admire Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the historic centro storico. Visit the Pantheon (free evening exterior viewing) and enjoy the lively atmosphere of the surrounding streets.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby bar – cornetto and cappuccino, the classic Roman start (~$5–8).
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the Vatican – try a local pizzeria al taglio (pizza by the slice) for an authentic, affordable bite (~$10–15).
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range trattoria near Piazza Navona or Campo de' Fiori. Try saltimbocca alla romana or abbacchio. Budget ~$25–35 per person including house wine.

day_by_day.notes: Vatican Museums tickets sell out weeks in advance – book online before your trip. Dress code enforced: covered shoulders and knees required for the Sistine Chapel. June heat (avg 29.8°C) means carry water and wear sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Borghese Gallery Art Experience (timed entry mandatory, book well in advance – only 360 visitors per 2-hour slot). Marvel at Bernini's breathtaking sculptures (Apollo and Daphne, The Rape of Proserpina) and Caravaggio's dramatic canvases in this intimate villa setting. One of Rome's finest art experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the gallery, enjoy the surrounding Villa Borghese gardens – rent a rowboat on the lake or simply relax in the shade. Walk or take a short taxi to the Spanish Steps and Via Condotti area for window shopping and people-watching.
day_by_day.evening: Trastevere Food & Wine Walking Tour (check operator schedules – many evening tours depart around 18:00–19:00). Wander Rome's most charming medieval neighborhood sampling supplì, artisanal cheeses, cured meats, and local wines with a knowledgeable guide.

meals.breakfast: Café near the hotel – cornetto integrale and a macchiato (~$5–8).
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch in Villa Borghese gardens – pick up fresh bread, cheese, and fruit from a nearby alimentari (deli). Budget ~$12–18.
meals.dinner: Included in the Trastevere Food & Wine Walking Tour (tastings count as dinner). Supplement with a final glass of wine at a Trastevere wine bar if still hungry. Budget tour cost ~$60–80 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery is considered Rome's best 'hidden gem' museum – the intimate scale makes it far more enjoyable than larger museums. Book both the gallery and the food tour as far in advance as possible. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the evening tour.

day_by_day.morning: Testaccio Market Culinary Exploration (market open from ~7:00 AM, best visited 9:00–11:30 AM before it winds down). Dive into Rome's most authentic food market – sample offal-based Roman street food, fresh produce, local cheeses, and artisan products. Chat with vendors and soak up the local atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Testaccio neighborhood on foot – visit the Non-Catholic Cemetery (Keats and Shelley are buried here, serene and beautiful), and see the Pyramid of Cestius. Then head to the Aventine Hill for the famous Knights of Malta keyhole view of St. Peter's dome and the peaceful Orange Garden (Giardino degli Aranci) with panoramic city views.
day_by_day.evening: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Sunset Visit (book timed entry; the combined ticket also covers the Colosseum). As golden hour light bathes the ancient ruins, walk through the heart of the Roman Empire. The Forum at sunset is magical and far less crowded than midday.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the Testaccio Market itself – this IS the breakfast experience. Try a supplì, a trapizzino, or a fresh cornetto from market vendors (~$8–12).
meals.lunch: Light lunch in Testaccio – the neighborhood has excellent, unpretentious trattorias. Try Da Remo for a classic Roman pizza or Flavio al Velavevodetto for hearty Roman cuisine. Budget ~$18–25 per person.
meals.dinner: After the sunset Forum visit, dine near the Colosseum area or head back toward the centro. Try a mid-range restaurant for classic Roman pasta dishes. Budget ~$25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Colosseum/Forum/Palatine Hill combined ticket must be booked in advance – Saturday is busy. The sunset slot (typically 17:00–19:00 entry) offers the best light and thinner crowds. Testaccio Market is closed Sundays, so today is the right day.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Colosseum (use your combined ticket from Day 4 if not yet used, or book separately). Explore the iconic amphitheater, including the arena floor if booked. Afterward, walk the exterior and photograph the arch of Constantine.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Capitoline Museums (world's oldest public museums) on Capitoline Hill – superb Roman sculpture collection including the original Marcus Aurelius equestrian statue and the Capitoline Wolf. The rooftop terrace offers stunning Forum views.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Jewish Ghetto neighborhood – one of Rome's oldest and most atmospheric quarters. Visit the Portico d'Ottavia ruins and enjoy the quiet Sunday evening streets.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local bar near the hotel (~$5–8).
meals.lunch: Lunch in the Jewish Ghetto area – try carciofi alla giudia (Jewish-style fried artichokes) and other Roman-Jewish specialties at a local restaurant. Budget ~$20–28 per person.
meals.dinner: Sunday evening in Rome – many locals dine out. Find a lively trattoria in the centro storico or Campo de' Fiori area. Try rigatoni alla pajata or coda alla vaccinara for adventurous Roman classics. Budget ~$25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Some museums and shops have reduced Sunday hours – check opening times in advance. The Capitoline Museums are often overlooked by tourists but are exceptional. June 33mm average rainfall means carry a compact umbrella – afternoon thunderstorms are possible.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Piazza del Popolo area – visit the twin baroque churches and the Egyptian obelisk. Walk up to the Pincian Hill terrace for sweeping panoramic views over Rome. Then visit the nearby Villa Medici gardens (check opening hours).
day_by_day.afternoon: Dedicated art afternoon: visit the Palazzo Doria Pamphilj (private family collection with Velázquez's portrait of Pope Innocent X and Caravaggio works – often uncrowded and excellent). Then wander through the elegant Via del Corso shopping street.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Trastevere independently (now that you know the neighborhood from the tour) for a relaxed evening. Explore the backstreets, pop into a local enoteca (wine bar) for a glass of natural Roman wine, and enjoy the bohemian atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Café near Piazza del Popolo – enjoy breakfast with a view at a bar on the piazza (~$6–10).
meals.lunch: Lunch near the Pantheon area – try Armando al Pantheon (book ahead, beloved local institution) or a nearby pizzeria. Budget ~$20–30 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Trastevere – choose from the many trattorias. Da Enzo al 29 or Tonnarello are beloved mid-range options. Try cacio e pepe or amatriciana. Budget ~$25–35 per person including wine.

day_by_day.notes: Monday can mean some museums are closed (check individual sites). Palazzo Doria Pamphilj is typically open Mondays – a great choice for today. The audio guide narrated by a family member is a charming touch. Stay hydrated in the June heat.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning – visit any missed highlights or revisit a favorite spot. Consider the Baths of Diocletian (part of the National Roman Museum, often uncrowded) near Termini, or simply enjoy a slow Roman breakfast at a classic bar, reading a newspaper like a local.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping – head to the artisan shops near Campo de' Fiori or Via del Governo Vecchio for unique, non-touristy gifts (leather goods, ceramics, local food products like pasta, olive oil, or bottarga). Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner – splurge slightly on your last night. Choose a well-regarded mid-range restaurant and order the full Roman experience: antipasto, primo (pasta), secondo (meat or fish), and finish with a tiramisu or panna cotta. Toast to a wonderful trip.

meals.breakfast: Slow, indulgent final breakfast at a historic Roman café – try Sant'Eustachio il Caffè for what many consider Rome's best espresso (~$5–8).
meals.lunch: Light lunch – a final supplì or pizza al taglio to save room for the farewell dinner (~$10–15).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a quality trattoria or osteria of your choice. Budget ~$35–50 per person for a celebratory final meal with a bottle of local Frascati or Cesanese wine.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your departure logistics tonight – taxi or transfer to the airport should be booked in advance, especially for early morning flights. Rome's traffic can be unpredictable. Allow extra time. Keep one change of clothes and essentials accessible if your main luggage is stored.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 16:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive Rome via Condor flight at 16:00. Clear customs, collect luggage, and transfer to La Quinta by Wyndham Rome. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll around the immediate hotel neighborhood to orient yourself and decompress from travel.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed welcome dinner at a nearby upscale Roman trattoria. Sip a Negroni at the hotel bar afterward and review the week ahead.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport)
meals.lunch: Not applicable (in-flight or airport)
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at a premium local trattoria near the hotel — try classic Roman pasta dishes such as Cacio e Pepe or Carbonara paired with a fine Frascati white wine.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Jet lag and travel fatigue are real — resist the urge to over-plan. Confirm all upcoming experience bookings (Vatican, Borghese, etc.) from your room this evening. Average high is ~30°C, so pack light breathable clothing and stay hydrated.

day_by_day.morning: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel — Begin with an exclusive early-access premium guided tour of the Vatican Museums, one of the world's greatest art collections. Explore the Gallery of Maps, Raphael Rooms, and culminate in Michelangelo's breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling. A private guide ensures you bypass the crowds and gain deep art-historical context.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Vatican, cross the Tiber and explore the elegant Prati neighborhood. Visit Castel Sant'Angelo for panoramic rooftop views of Rome. Browse the upscale boutiques along Via Cola di Rienzo before heading back to the hotel to rest during the hottest part of the day (~30°C peak).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset aperitivo on a rooftop bar overlooking St. Peter's dome, followed by a premium dinner in Prati featuring modern Roman cuisine with seasonal ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Full Italian breakfast at the hotel or a nearby high-end café — cornetto, cappuccino, fresh-squeezed orange juice.
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the Vatican — a gourmet panino or a sit-down meal at a refined Prati enoteca with local wines.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a celebrated Prati restaurant such as Il Sorpasso or equivalent — Roman artichokes, saltimbocca alla Romana, and a bottle of Cesanese del Piglio red wine.

day_by_day.notes: Book Vatican early-access tickets well in advance — they sell out weeks ahead. Dress code enforced: covered shoulders and knees required inside the Vatican. Carry a light scarf. Bring water and sunscreen for the afternoon walk.

day_by_day.morning: Borghese Gallery Art Experience — Enjoy an intimate, timed-entry premium visit to the Borghese Gallery, home to Bernini's stunning baroque sculptures (Apollo and Daphne, The Rape of Proserpina) and Caravaggio's dramatic masterworks. A private art expert guide will illuminate the stories behind each piece in this jewel-box villa setting.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the gallery, take a leisurely walk through the lush Villa Borghese gardens — Rome's green lung. Rent a rowboat on the lake or simply relax in the shade. Head to the Spanish Steps area and explore the luxury shopping streets of Via Condotti (Valentino, Bulgari, Fendi) for an indulgent afternoon browse.
day_by_day.evening: Aperitivo hour at a chic rooftop bar near the Trevi Fountain, then a gourmet dinner in the upscale Tridente neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the iconic Antico Caffè Greco on Via Condotti — Rome's oldest café, serving since 1760. Espresso and pastries in historic surroundings.
meals.lunch: Elegant lunch at a garden restaurant in the Parioli district near Villa Borghese — seasonal Roman cuisine with a curated wine list.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a Michelin-recognized restaurant in the Tridente area — tasting menu featuring creative interpretations of Roman classics, paired with sommelier-selected Italian wines.

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery strictly limits visitors to 2-hour timed slots — advance booking is mandatory and premium guided slots fill quickly. The gallery is closed Mondays. Morning is the coolest and best time to visit. Wear comfortable shoes for the garden walk.

day_by_day.morning: Testaccio Market Culinary Exploration — Immerse yourself in Rome's most authentic food culture at the beloved Testaccio Market. Join a premium guided culinary tour sampling offal-based Roman street food (supplì, porchetta, trippa), artisan cheeses, cured meats, and seasonal produce. Meet local vendors and learn about the deep culinary traditions of this working-class Roman neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Testaccio neighborhood on foot — visit the Non-Catholic Cemetery (where Keats and Shelley are buried), the ancient Pyramid of Cestius, and the vibrant street art of the Ostiense district. Return to the hotel for a mid-afternoon rest during peak heat.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Testaccio, the undisputed culinary heart of Rome, at one of its legendary trattorias known for nose-to-tail Roman cooking.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a quick espresso and cornetto at a neighborhood bar before heading to Testaccio.
meals.lunch: The market tour itself serves as a progressive tasting lunch — supplì, cured meats, cheeses, seasonal vegetables, and local wine included in the premium experience.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Flavio al Velavevodetto or Da Remo (Testaccio classics) — rigatoni alla pajata, coda alla vaccinara, and tiramisu, paired with a robust Montepulciano d'Abruzzo.

day_by_day.notes: Testaccio Market is best visited in the morning when produce and vendors are at their freshest. Wear comfortable walking shoes. The neighborhood is authentic and less touristy — a genuine Roman experience. June heat peaks in the afternoon, so the mid-day rest is strongly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Morning Visit — Explore the ancient heart of the Roman Empire with a premium private guided tour of the Roman Forum and Palatine Hill. Walk among millennia-old ruins where Julius Caesar once stood, explore the imperial palaces on Palatine Hill, and gain expert insight into the rise and fall of the greatest empire in history.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Forum, visit the Colosseum with your combined ticket (included). Opt for an underground and arena floor premium access tour for an extraordinary perspective. Afterward, cool down with a gelato from a premium artisan gelateria nearby and explore the Celio neighborhood's hidden medieval churches.
day_by_day.evening: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Sunset Visit — Return to the Forum area at golden hour for the magical sunset experience as warm light bathes the ancient ruins. Enjoy a private sunset aperitivo with a view, then dinner in the elegant Aventine Hill neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast to fuel a full day of walking.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a refined restaurant near the Colosseum — avoid tourist traps and opt for a pre-booked table at a quality enoteca in the Celio district.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a premium Aventine Hill restaurant with terrace views — Roman cuisine elevated with fine ingredients, excellent natural wines, and impeccable service.

day_by_day.notes: This is the most physically demanding day — comfortable walking shoes are essential. Start the morning tour early (8:00–8:30 AM) before the heat and crowds build. Carry at least 1.5L of water. The sunset visit is a separate, magical experience worth the return trip — book a premium sunset access slot in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Trastevere Food & Wine Walking Tour — Wander through Rome's most enchanting medieval neighborhood on a premium guided food and wine tour. Sample supplì (fried rice balls), artisan cheeses, cured meats, and local wines while exploring cobblestone alleys, ivy-draped piazzas, and centuries-old basilicas. Visit the stunning Santa Maria in Trastevere basilica with its glittering 12th-century mosaics.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the tour, explore Trastevere at your own pace — browse artisan boutiques, visit the Botanical Garden of Rome for a shaded respite, and cross the Tiber to explore the Jewish Ghetto and its unique culinary heritage (Jewish-Roman artichokes are a must-try). Visit the Pantheon in the late afternoon when crowds thin.
day_by_day.evening: Final premium dinner in Trastevere — the neighborhood transforms beautifully at night with candlelit restaurants and a romantic atmosphere. Enjoy a digestivo passeggiata along the Tiber.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a charming Trastevere café before the tour begins — fresh cornetti, maritozzi con la panna, and excellent espresso.
meals.lunch: The Trastevere food tour serves as a progressive tasting lunch with wine pairings included in the premium experience.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a top Trastevere restaurant such as Da Enzo al 29 or Glass Hostaria (Michelin-starred) — exceptional Roman cuisine in an intimate medieval setting, with a curated Italian wine list.

day_by_day.notes: Trastevere is best explored on foot — no cars in most of the neighborhood. The food tour typically runs 3–4 hours. Book the evening restaurant well in advance as top Trastevere spots fill up quickly, especially on weekends. Carry a light cardigan for the evening as temperatures drop pleasantly after sunset.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Rome — enjoy a slow, indulgent Italian breakfast at the hotel. Take a last leisurely walk to a nearby piazza for a farewell espresso standing at the bar, as Romans do. Visit a nearby luxury food shop (such as a premium deli or enoteca) to pick up artisan food souvenirs — aged Pecorino Romano, truffle products, premium olive oil, or fine Italian wines to take home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel. Depending on departure time, enjoy a final light lunch near the hotel before transferring to the airport. Reflect on an extraordinary week of art, food, and la dolce vita.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Rome. Buon viaggio!

meals.breakfast: Luxurious final Italian breakfast — a spread of pastries, fresh fruit, cold cuts, cheeses, and excellent coffee at the hotel or a premium nearby café.
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch — a beautifully crafted Roman sandwich (panino) or a quick sit-down meal at a quality neighborhood restaurant near the hotel.
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination.

day_by_day.notes: Allow ample time for airport transfer — Rome traffic can be unpredictable, especially in summer. Pack any purchased food items carefully per airline regulations (liquids, cured meats, and cheeses have specific rules for international travel). Consider a private car transfer to the airport for a premium, stress-free departure experience.
